doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: Her music, free jazz and playing
title: What free jazz means
summary: Prompted by Roscoe Mitchell's remark, she says she cannot define free music but still gravitates to structure.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: Let’s talk about that out a bit. Yesterday I did an interview with Roscoe Mitchell. And I didn’t even — it wasn’t a question but I said something about free jazz. And he was adamant there’s no such thing as free jazz. And I think the reason, well he said it, he says considering how hard I work at this music there’s no such thing as free jazz — and he was almost angry about it. For you, what does free actually mean?

Wow. That is a very deep question. Wow. I’m not sure how to answer that. That is such a wide question. Because if I say okay free means we’re not playing a tune or we’re not playing over a structure, but that’s actually not true either because while I’m playing free music in my head I create a structure and I create something. I create, it’s just a spontaneous structure that I play off of. I can’t answer it, I wish I could. How did he answer it?

I can’t answer it either but I’ve noticed, I’m not necessarily a person who has listened to a great deal of it but going back to “Ascension” and some of the music I listened to that Mr. Mitchell had recorded, that it seemed like, you have to be careful with generalities in music but it seemed like the majority of free jazz for one thing did not have a steady tempo, especially from the drums and bass. In other words we’re freeing ourselves from that role that we normally play.

I guess we’re freeing ourselves from playing, from doing these things like playing rhythm, playing melody, playing harmony, in that certain way but we still use time, we still use rhythm and melody and harmony but just not in a preconceived way I guess. But when I play free music I always tend, I gravitate toward certain things. My ear just takes me there. I just, to me, when I play free music then I begin to knit, if you will, a series of changes that I don’t share with the others. They follow or they don’t follow but I still — my ear still wants to go to some things that I recognize. So it’s — to define what free music is I wouldn’t dare.
